bib.title: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network

question: Can the knowledge in a large, cumbersome model or ensemble be transferred to a single small model that is cheap to deploy, and can ensembles of specialists cut ensemble training cost on very large datasets?
hypothesis: A small model trained to match the softened class probabilities of a cumbersome model generalizes much better than the same small model trained on hard labels alone.
contributions: Distillation: train a small model on soft targets from a high-temperature softmax of a cumbersome model, showing logit matching is a special case
Distilling a 10-model ensemble into one model for a commercial speech acoustic model
A new ensemble of one generalist plus many specialist models trained in parallel, evaluated on JFT
Soft targets as regularizers: recovering most of full-data accuracy from 3% of the data

method.summary: Soft targets from a cumbersome model (ensemble or regularized net) at temperature T train a small model with a weighted sum of soft-target cross-entropy (scaled by T^2) and hard-label cross-entropy; the small model uses T=1 at test time. Tested on MNIST, an Android-voice-search-like acoustic model, and JFT specialist ensembles.
method.task: knowledge distillation / model compression (classification: MNIST digits, speech frame classification, image classification)

datasets.name: MNIST
datasets.preprocessing: inputs jittered by up to two pixels in any direction for the large net

datasets.name: Internal speech data (English, Android voice search)
datasets.split: dev set for frame accuracy and WER; WER test set of 23K words
datasets.preprocessing: 26 frames of 40 Mel-scaled filterbank coefficients, 10ms advance, predicting HMM state of 21st frame; labels from forced alignment

datasets.name: JFT
datasets.split: development set (Table 3) and test set (Table 4, per-row counts); sizes not otherwise stated

models.name: MNIST large net
models.architecture: MLP, 2 hidden layers of 1200 ReLU units, dropout and weight constraints

models.name: MNIST small net
models.architecture: MLP, 2 hidden layers of 800 ReLU units, no regularization; also 300+ and 30 units per layer variants

models.name: Speech DNN acoustic model (baseline, each ensemble member, and distilled model)
models.architecture: 8 hidden layers of 2560 ReLU units, softmax over 14,000 HMM-target labels; slightly outdated version of Android voice search model
models.init_from: random; ensemble members differ in random initialization

models.name: JFT generalist
models.architecture: deep convolutional neural network, trained about six months with asynchronous SGD

models.name: JFT specialists
models.architecture: generalist copy with softmax over its 300 special classes plus one dustbin class

training.objective: weighted average of cross-entropy with soft targets (teacher and student both at temperature T, gradient multiplied by T^2) and cross-entropy with correct labels at T=1, with considerably lower weight on the hard-label term; specialists: half examples from special subset, half random, dustbin logit corrected by log of oversampling proportion
training.optimizer: distributed stochastic gradient descent (speech); asynchronous SGD with sharded parameter server (JFT baseline)
training.dropout: large MNIST net strongly regularized with dropout
training.regularisation: MNIST large net: dropout and weight constraints; early stopping used for 3% hard-label speech baseline
training.hardware: large number of cores with model and data parallelism (JFT baseline)
training.compute: JFT baseline about six months; specialists a few days
training.wall_clock: JFT baseline about six months; specialists a few days instead of many weeks

other.mnist_temperature: 20 for 800-unit student; 8 or above similar for 300+ units; 2.5 to 4 best for 30 units
other.transfer_set: original training set used for speech; MNIST transfer sets with digit 3 omitted, or only 7s and 8s
other.ensemble_size_speech: 10 models, same architecture and procedure, different random init
other.ensemble_soft_targets: arithmetic or geometric mean of members' distributions
other.specialist_clustering: online K-means on columns of covariance matrix of generalist predictions

inference.decoding: distilled model uses temperature 1 after training; speech decoder searches HMM path with language model
inference.samples: single run per setting; no seeds or repeats reported

parameters.active_specialists: those whose class subset intersects the top-n set
parameters.combination: find q minimizing KL(pg,q)+sum over active specialists KL(pm,q) by gradient descent on logits z, q=softmax(z), T=1, per image

metrics.name: Frame accuracy
metrics.definition: frame-level classification accuracy of HMM state

metrics.name: WER
metrics.definition: word error rate on 23K-word test set

metrics.name: Top-1 accuracy / conditional test accuracy (JFT)
metrics.definition: conditional = accuracy considering only examples in specialist classes and restricting predictions to that subset

baselines: Same architecture trained on hard labels
Li et al. 2014 distillation at T=1 with unlabeled data
eval.protocol: Single reported numbers; no variance, seeds or significance tests stated.

availability.data: internal Google data (JFT, speech); MNIST public

evidence.quote: used a relative weight of 0.5 on the cross-entropy for the hard targets

results.claim: Distilled single speech model recovers most of the ensemble's frame-accuracy gain (60.8% vs 61.1% ensemble vs 58.9% baseline).
results.setup: 85M-parameter DNN acoustic model (8x2560 ReLU, 14,000 HMM-state softmax), ~2000 h English speech, ~700M frames; 10-model ensemble distilled at best of T in [1,2,5,10], hard weight 0.5
results.table: Table 1, row Distilled Single model, column Test Frame Accuracy
results.note: Gain recovered (60.8-58.9)/(61.1-58.9)=86% by my arithmetic; paper says 'More than 80%' for frame accuracy, not WER.

results.claim: More than 80% of the ensemble's frame-accuracy improvement transfers to the distilled model.
results.setup: 85M-parameter DNN acoustic model (8x2560 ReLU, 14,000 HMM-state softmax), ~2000 h English speech, ~700M frames
results.quote:
More than 80% of the improvement in frame classiﬁcation accuracy achieved by using an ensemble of 10 models is trans-
ferred to the distilled model
results.note: Applies to frame accuracy; WER gain is small (10.9 -> 10.7 for both).

results.setup: 85M-parameter DNN acoustic model (8x2560 ReLU, 14,000 HMM-state softmax), ~2000 h English speech, ~700M frames
results.table: Table 1, row 10xEnsemble, column Test Frame Accuracy

results.claim: Distilled model and ensemble both reach 10.7% WER vs 10.9% baseline.
results.setup: 85M-parameter DNN acoustic model (8x2560 ReLU, 14,000 HMM-state softmax), ~2000 h English speech, ~700M frames; dev set
results.table: Table 1, row Distilled Single model, column WER

results.claim: With 3% of the speech data, hard-label training overfits to 44.5% test frame accuracy (early stopping).

results.quote: the accuracy drops sharply after reaching 44.5%

results.claim: With 3% of the data, soft targets from the full-data model give 57.0% test frame accuracy without early stopping.

results.table: Table 5, row Soft Targets (3% of training set), column Test Frame Accuracy

results.setup: 85M-parameter DNN acoustic model (8x2560 ReLU, 14,000 HMM-state softmax), ~2000 h English speech, ~700M frames
results.quote: This system achieves a frame accuracy of 58.9%, and a Word Error Rate (WER) of 10.9%

results.claim: MNIST: small net distilled at T=20 gets 74 test errors vs 146 without and 67 for the large regularized net.
results.setup: MNIST 60,000 train; teacher 2x1200 ReLU with dropout; student 2x800 ReLU, no regularization other than soft targets

results.claim: MNIST with no 3s in transfer set: 206 errors, 109 after raising 3's bias by 3.5; 98.6% of test 3s correct.

results.quote: the distilled model gets 98.6% of the test 3s correct
results.note: Bias tuned on the test set.

With 61 specialist models, there is a 4.4% relative improvement in test ac-

results.table: Table 3, row + 61 Specialist models, column Conditional Test Accuracy

limits: Specialists were not distilled back into a single net: 'We have not yet shown that we can distill the knowledge in the specialists back into the single large net.'
No seeds, variance or significance tests; hyperparameters (lr, batch size, steps) not given; JFT and speech data are internal.
Ensemble WER gain is small (10.9 to 10.7), attributed to objective mismatch.
MNIST bias corrections tuned on the test set.
Using specialists with a full softmax and soft targets to prevent overfitting was only proposed, still being explored.

terms.definition: raise the temperature of the final softmax until the cumbersome model produces a suitably soft set of targets, then use the same high temperature when training the small model
class probabilities produced by the cumbersome model used as training targets for the small model
the set used to train the distilled model, unlabeled data or the original training set
a single class combining all classes a specialist does not care about
accuracy considering only examples belonging to the specialist classes, restricting predictions to that subset
